hook.situation: A friend says they cannot come, cannot eat meat, or do not want something. Korean needs different negative forms depending on whether the issue is choice, ability, absence, or careful clarification.
objectives: Choose 안 for simple choice or ordinary negation.
Choose 못 when something blocks the action: schedule, ability, rule, or health.
Use 없다 for absence and -지 않아요 for careful or more formal negation.
hook.whyItMatters: English 'not' hides several different Korean meanings. 안 가요 can sound like you are choosing not to go, while 못 가요 says you cannot go because something blocks you. That difference matters when declining invitations or explaining food restrictions.

grammarNotes.title: 안 + verb/adjective — simple not; often choice or fact
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 안 is the quick everyday negative. With actions, it can sound like you simply do not do it or are choosing not to.
grammarNotes.formation: Put 안 before most verbs/adjectives. With noun + 하다 verbs, 안 usually goes between the noun and 하다: 공부 안 해요, 운동 안 해요.

examples.en: I am not going today.
examples.note: Can sound like a choice or decision.

examples.en: I do not eat meat.
examples.note: Often heard as preference, habit, or choice unless a reason is added.

examples.en: I do not exercise these days.
I will not call today.

exceptions: 안 is not the best choice when the action is impossible because of a real restriction. Use 못: 알레르기가 있어서 못 먹어요.
Some fixed adjective pairs prefer 아니다 or 없다 rather than 안.

grammarNotes.title: 못 + verb — cannot because something blocks it
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 못 says the action is blocked. The block may be ability, time, rules, health, money, or circumstances.
grammarNotes.formation: Put 못 before the verb: 못 가요, 못 먹어요. With noun + 하다 verbs, use noun 못 해요 or 못 해요: 예약 못 해요, 공부 못 해요.

examples.en: I cannot go to the gathering today.
examples.note: The speaker is blocked, not simply refusing.

examples.en: I cannot go because of overtime.
examples.note: The reason supports the 못 reading.

examples.en: I cannot eat meat because I have an allergy.
I cannot call right now.

exceptions: 못 does not mean 'I do not want to.' If the point is desire, use 안, 싫다, or -고 싶지 않다.
한국어를 잘 못해요 is a fixed useful frame for limited ability.

grammarNotes.title: -지 않아요 — careful, written, or clarifying negation
grammarNotes.mentalModel: This is the longer negative. It is useful when you want to sound careful, written, or precise rather than quick and casual.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -지 않아요 to a verb or adjective stem: 가다 → 가지 않아요, 먹다 → 먹지 않아요, 어렵다 → 어렵지 않아요.

examples.ko: 가기 싫은 건 아니에요. 싫지 않아요.
examples.romanization: gagi silheun geon anieyo. silhji anayo.
examples.en: It is not that I do not want to go. I do not dislike it.
This task is not difficult.
I do not eat meat.
examples.note: More careful or written than 고기 안 먹어요.

examples.en: I decided not to go today.
examples.note: -지 않다 can combine with other grammar.

exceptions: -지 않아요 does not automatically mean inability. For inability, use 못.
In casual speech, short 안 is often more natural unless you need careful clarification.

grammarNotes.title: N이/가 없어요 — absence; do not have
grammarNotes.mentalModel: 없어요 negates existence or possession. It says the thing is absent, not that an action is refused.
grammarNotes.formation: N이/가 없어요. Use 이 after consonant-final nouns and 가 after vowel-final nouns.

examples.en: I do not have time.
examples.note: The absence of time explains 못 가요.

examples.en: I cannot reserve because I do not have money.
examples.note: 없다 names the missing resource; 못 names the blocked action.

examples.en: There is no way.
I do not have an allergy.

exceptions: Do not use 안 있다 for ordinary 'do not have.' Say 없어요.
없어요 can be the reason for 못, but it is not the same form: 시간이 없어서 못 가요.

grammarNotes.title: Boundary check — 안 vs 못 vs 싫다 vs 아니에요
grammarNotes.mentalModel: Before choosing a negative, ask what is being denied: the action, the ability, the desire, the existence, or the identity.
grammarNotes.formation: Use 안 for simple action negation, 못 for blocked action, 싫다 or -고 싶지 않다 for dislike/lack of desire, 없다 for absence, and 아니다/아니에요 for 'is not.'

examples.en: I am not going.
I cannot go.
I do not want to go.
It is not that I do not want to go.

exceptions: A polite refusal may avoid a direct negative: 오늘은 좀 어려울 것 같아요 can mean 'I probably cannot make it.'
Do not translate every English 'not' into 안.

exampleSentence.ko: 안 가는 거예요, 아니면 못 가는 거예요?
exampleSentence.en: Are you choosing not to go, or are you unable to go?
I cannot eat meat because I have an allergy.
I do not exercise these days.
I cannot go because I do not have time.
I cannot go because of overtime.
I cannot eat it because I have an allergy.
It is not that I do not want to go.
I will reserve a different menu so it is not difficult.
I do not exercise these days.

extendedDialogue.setting: A friend clarifies whether a refusal is about choice, schedule, or a real restriction.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 오늘 모임에는 못 가요. 시간이 없어요.
lines.romanization: oneul moimeneun mot gayo. sigani eopseoyo.
lines.en: I cannot go to the gathering today. I do not have time.
lines.grammarNote: 못 marks the blocked action; 시간이 없어요 gives the absent resource.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 안 가는 거예요, 아니면 정말 못 가는 거예요?
lines.romanization: an ganeun geoyeyo, animyeon jeongmal mot ganeun geoyeyo?
lines.en: Are you choosing not to go, or are you really unable to go?
lines.grammarNote: This line directly contrasts 안 and 못.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 가기 싫은 건 아니에요. 야근 때문에 못 가요.
lines.romanization: gagi silheun geon anieyo. yageun ttaemune mot gayo.
lines.en: It is not that I do not want to go. I cannot go because of overtime.
lines.grammarNote: 아니에요 rejects the claim; 못 gives the real reason.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Then at the company dinner, do you not eat meat?
lines.grammarNote: 안 먹어요 asks about habit, choice, or preference.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 싫어서 안 먹는 게 아니라 알레르기가 있어서 못 먹어요.
lines.romanization: silheoseo an meongneun ge anira allereugiga isseoseo mot meogeoyo.
lines.en: It is not that I avoid it because I dislike it; I cannot eat it because I have an allergy.
lines.grammarNote: 알레르기 makes 못 the right choice.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.ko: 그럼 어렵지 않게 다른 메뉴로 예약할게요.
lines.romanization: geureom eoryeopji anke dareun menyuro yeyakhalgeyo.
lines.en: Then I will reserve a different menu so it is not difficult.
lines.grammarNote: -지 않게 gives a careful adjective negation.

readingText.title: 안 가요와 못 가요는 같은 말이 아니에요
readingText.body: 친구의 초대를 거절할 때 '안 가요'와 '못 가요'는 느낌이 달라요. '안 가요'는 내가 가지 않기로 한 선택처럼 들릴 수 있고, '못 가요'는 시간, 일, 건강 같은 이유 때문에 갈 수 없다는 뜻이에요. 그래서 '시간이 없어서 못 가요'라고 말하면 오해가 줄어요. 음식도 마찬가지예요. '고기는 안 먹어요'는 취향이나 습관처럼 들릴 수 있지만, '알레르기가 있어서 못 먹어요'는 몸의 제한을 설명해요. 더 조심스럽게 말하고 싶을 때는 '싫지 않아요', '어렵지 않아요', '먹지 않아요'처럼 -지 않아요를 쓸 수 있어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: When declining an invitation, 안 가요 and 못 가요 do not feel the same. 안 가요 can sound like a choice, while 못 가요 says you cannot go because of time, work, health, or another limit. Food works similarly: 고기는 안 먹어요 may sound like preference or habit, but 알레르기가 있어서 못 먹어요 explains a physical restriction. For careful clarification, use -지 않아요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 안 가요는 어떤 느낌으로 들릴 수 있어요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 내가 가지 않기로 한 선택처럼 들릴 수 있어요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 알레르기가 있을 때 왜 못 먹어요가 자연스러워요?
comprehensionQuestions.answer: 취향이 아니라 몸의 제한 때문에 먹을 수 없다는 뜻이기 때문이에요.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 조심스럽게 부정하거나 설명할 때 어떤 형태를 쓸 수 있어요?

culturalNote.title: Soft refusals often hide the exact negative
culturalNote.body: Korean speakers often soften refusals with phrases like 오늘은 좀 어려울 것 같아요 instead of a blunt 안 가요 or 못 가요. That phrase may mean 'I cannot make it' without naming the full reason. Still, when you do give a reason, choosing 안, 못, 없다, or -지 않다 correctly prevents misunderstanding.
culturalNote.tip: If the listener might think you simply do not want to, add the reason: 시간이 없어서 못 가요, 알레르기가 있어서 못 먹어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence says circumstances make it impossible to go?
inlineExercises.explanation: 못 marks inability or a blocked situation.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence best explains a medical food restriction?
inlineExercises.explanation: 알레르기 is an outside restriction, so 못 먹어요 is natural.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence uses absence as the reason?
inlineExercises.explanation: 없어요 negates the existence/possession of time.

inlineExercises.prompt: Careful adjective negation: 이 일은 어렵____ 않아요.
Which pair correctly contrasts choice and inability?
inlineExercises.explanation: 안 often marks not doing or choosing not to; 못 marks inability or blocked action.

bullets: 안: simple negative or choice, as in 오늘은 안 가요.
못: blocked action or inability, as in 시간이 없어서 못 가요.
-지 않아요: careful or written negation, as in 어렵지 않아요.
없어요: absence or not having, as in 시간이 없어요.
Do not translate every English 'not' the same way. Decide what is being denied.
